# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 80 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 80 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_080_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 8 — More Trees Explained

**1** He showed me many more trees — some putting out fresh buds, others completely dried out. **2** "Do you see these trees?" he asked. "Yes, Lord," I answered. "The ones that are budding and putting out shoots," he said, "represent those who are going to repent and come back to life. The Lord saw their turning back and decided to give them another chance at life. **3** But the ones that are dried out and bear no fruit — they have inwardly walked away from God. They will not turn back to repentance, nor return to the land of the living." **4** "But Lord," I said, "why did you place some of the dried-out ones among those who were repenting?" "So that when they see the joy on the faces of those turning back to God, they might be ashamed and repent themselves," he explained. "If they witness the transformation of people who hadn't known the Lord before but now do — they might repent wholeheartedly." **5** "And if they still don't repent?" I asked. "Then they will die," he said. "Those who refuse to repent at that point are lost. But those who did repent and lived rightly will live with God. Those who refused and stayed in their wicked ways will perish." **6** "What about those who returned completely green but cracked branches?" I asked. "These were always genuinely faithful and good people — but they were eaten up by rivalry with each other over status and recognition. It's quite foolish, really, quarreling over who gets the honor." **7** "And those who returned half-withered and cracked branches?" **8** "These are people who were believers but became wealthy and gained social standing among unbelievers. Their success bred arrogance — they became proud and cut themselves off from the truth. They stopped associating with other believers and adapted to the lifestyle of the surrounding culture, which appealed to them. They didn't completely abandon God — they held onto their faith — but they stopped actually living it out. **9** Many of them did repent, though some stayed on their old path. Those who received their branches with some life still in them hadn't let go of the living God entirely, and his name had never left their lips. That's why their branches still had some moisture."

---

*PNEUMA translates the socioeconomic critique embedded in Hermas's vision — the danger of wealth and social assimilation — into direct contemporary terms.*
